strings.options.tab.desc: Left and Right switch between the GENERAL tab, for settings shared by every game, and each game's own tab, with its display settings and the rules for new games.
strings.options.window_scale.desc: How many times the game's 320x200 picture is enlarged in a window, from 1 to 6. F11 also steps through the sizes. Applies to every game.
strings.options.start_maximized.desc: ON opens the window maximized; the picture still grows by whole steps, with borders around it. OFF opens a window at the WINDOW SCALE size. Applies to every game.
strings.options.import_games.desc: Opens the import screen: point it at your own copy of a game (disk images, zip files, an installed folder, or your Steam or GOG library) and it builds the game's data, maps, text and pictures from it. Import a second version later (for example the Amiga disk after the DOS one) to add its pictures.
strings.options.update.at_start.desc: ON asks the OpenPhantasie releases page for a newer version each time the game starts (it needs an internet connection and sends nothing but the request). When there is one, the update screen opens with its notes; you choose whether to update. OFF never checks by itself; UPDATE NOW still does. Local builds (not a release download) never check.
strings.options.update.now_row.desc: Shows the version you are running and checks for a newer one now. If there is one, its notes show and UPDATE NOW downloads it, puts it over this copy of the game and restarts. Your settings, saves and imported games are kept (they are in your user data folder, not the game's folder). Only from the main menu.

strings.options.graphics.desc: Which platform's artwork this game is drawn with, for example AMIGA. Only a game with more than one graphics set can change it. Graphics never change the rules.
strings.options.diagonal_moves.desc: ON lets the numpad's 7, 9, 1 and 3 (or Home, PgUp, End, PgDn), or the pad's left stick pushed on a slant, step diagonally on the wilderness and dungeon maps, as two ordinary steps. OFF keeps the manual's four directions.
strings.options.status_lines.desc: ON adds the remaster's status line (mode, gold, party, region, position, days out) and a key help line to the wilderness and dungeon screens. OFF shows the original screens.
strings.options.continue_from_list.desc: ON makes Continue list the saved parties (leader, size, where they are) to pick from, with a last row that still asks for a Guild number. OFF asks for the Guild number of a character, as the original does.
strings.options.save_slots.desc: ON gives the game numbered save slots beside its autosave: Save and Load show a list of the slots with each one's party, place and date, a slot that holds a save asks before it is overwritten, and picking the game on the main menu offers its saves. Phantasie I-III have nine slots and the AUTO slot that leaving a town writes (when the game autosaves); Phantasie IV always has its original's three slots: ON shows them in this list, OFF on the original's own Save screen (System, then Save). OFF keeps the one save Phantasie I-III have always had (the AUTO slot). Turning it on or off changes no save.
strings.options.inventory_screen.desc: ON makes the inventory key open the remaster's paperdoll and stash screen. OFF shows the original item lists. Where items may be moved is a rule of the save; elsewhere the screen is read-only. A save with MODERN INVENTORY always uses the new screen.
strings.options.original_screens.desc: ON shows the Amiga's own screens, as the original: each combat round on the Amiga's field, the monsters above the party's portraits, one line at a time (I: in orange under the party; III: party lines blue, monster lines red), the attacker's swing frame before its line and the sounds; I's orders window and menu strip; III's Bank and Trade windows. OFF shows the remaster's combat screen with a round's lines at once and its own dialogs.
strings.options.combat_speed.desc: The original's Speed menu for combat. I and III (Amiga field): NORMAL holds each line 0.6 seconds, SLOW twice as long, FAST a quarter. II (Atari ST): a line holds 10 ms at NORMAL, 1 second at SLOW, 5 ms at FAST, and at NORMAL and SLOW each sound waits for the one before. Shift still skips the fight.
strings.options.title_screen.desc: ON shows the game's own title pictures when you pick the game, in the order and for the time the original showed them at start-up. A key or click ends a picture (one the original held until a key, or for a time not yet known, stays until then); Esc skips them all. OFF goes straight to the game.
strings.options.title_tune.desc: ON plays the tune the original played under its title pictures, decoded from the original's own file and played on a model of its sound chip: I the Amiga tamb.dat (cover1 lasts the tune), II the Atari ST start-up sound, III the Amiga D/m0, IV the X68000 FM song (OPMDRV on a YM2151 model). A key that ends the tune's picture ends the tune. OFF shows the pictures silently, each for the same time. Needs TITLE SCREEN on; with no sound device the game runs silently.
strings.options.a500_filter.desc: ON plays the Amiga's sounds (the title tune, the sound effects, III's reward tune) through a model of the Amiga 500's analogue output filters, with the power-LED low-pass filter in as the original leaves it: the warmer, duller sound of the real machine. OFF plays the sound chip's raw output, brighter and sharper. A sound already playing keeps the old setting; the next one takes the new. Only the Amiga's sounds; the other machines' sounds are not changed.
strings.options.colorblind.desc: ON swaps the colours that are hard to tell apart with red-green colour blindness: status and hit point colours, map colours and some art. OFF leaves every colour as the original drew it.
strings.options.auto_map.desc: ON shows a small map of the whole dungeon level in a corner of the dungeon view, away from the party and never over the party pictures: the cells you have seen, and the party in cyan. A click on a cell walks there. Tab hides or shows it in the dungeon, and changes this setting. OFF shows the dungeon as the original does, with no box.
strings.options.terrain_key.desc: ON shows a terrain key beside the wilderness map, as the rulebook prints one: each terrain's fill pattern or map symbol with its name from the manual. The party pictures share the space beside the map with it, and both scroll when they don't fit: the mouse wheel or bar, [ and ] for the party, comma and period for the key (pad: right stick for the party, right trigger + right stick for the key). OFF shows the map as the Atari ST does, with no key.
strings.options.mystic_skip.desc: ON lets Space, Return, a click or the pad's A button end the Mystic's reading at once instead of waiting about 23 seconds. The picture and the reading are the same either way; only the wait is skipped. OFF plays the reading as the original does, reading no keys until it has finished.
strings.options.common_town_keys.desc: ON gives every game the same town letters, the Phantasie I manual's: A Armory, B Bank, G Guild, M Mystic, N Inn, L Leave, C Cast, U Use, D Distribute, I Inspect, S Save, plus T Trade. In III they replace the Amiga menu bar's letters (G is then the Guild, not Trade); its other keys still work. In IV they open the doors this town has, I shows a profile and S saves; the digits and IV's own keys still work. OFF keeps each game's own keys. Phantasie I and II already use this set.
strings.options.time_lag_where.desc: Where the combat speed (time lag) and sound are set. T COMMAND: with the manual's T command in the wilderness and dungeon. IN OPTIONS: as TIME LAG and SOUND rows just below, changed any time, and T is no command.
strings.options.time_lag.desc: The pause before each round of combat is shown: 0 is the fastest, 9 the slowest. Changes pacing only, not the game.
strings.options.sound.desc: Turns the game's sound effects on or off.
strings.options.preset.desc: A ready-made set of rules for new games. ORIGINAL (MANUAL) follows the 1986 manual. ORIGINAL (DOS), (ATARI ST) or (X68000) plays as that original version's code. REMASTER is the manual plus recommended conveniences. CUSTOM is any other mix. Rules lock into a save when a new game starts.

strings.option.p1.elemental-prep.desc: How strong the elemental from SUMMON ELEMENTAL is. FULL STATS: it fights with its own attack, damage and armor, as the manual's 'to fight for the party' implies. ZERO STATS: the DOS bug, where it fights with zero attack, damage and armor.
strings.option.p1.stash-access.desc: Where you can open the found-item stash and move items between members. IN TOWN: only in town, as in the original game. ANYWHERE: anywhere outside combat, a convenience the original never had.
strings.option.p1.armory-restock.desc: Which Armory goods can sell out or vanish between town visits. WEAPONS, POTIONS: only weapons and potions come and go, as the manual says; armor and shields stay, and a sold-out piece can return. ARMOR TOO: as in the DOS game, armor and shields can also be wiped or cut to one.
strings.option.p1.gold-cap.desc: The most gold the party purse and each bank account can hold; gold over the cap is lost. 65,000: the manual's limit. 65,535: the DOS game's limit. NO CAP: no practical limit.
strings.option.p1.rename-party.desc: Whether the Guild can rename a character who is in a party. NO: refused, as the manual says ('Characters cannot be renamed while they are members of a party'). YES: allowed, as the DOS game does.
strings.option.p1.stunning-blow.desc: What a monster's stunning blow does to the member it hits. SURVIVORS ONLY: only a member who lives through the hit is stunned; the dead stay dead. THE DEAD TOO: as in DOS, a member the hit kills is put to sleep at 0 HP, counts as alive and can die again.
strings.option.p1.armor-reduced.desc: What a monster attack that says 'THE PARTY'S ARMOR IS REDUCED' really lowers. LOWERS ARMOR: the party's armor, as the message says, so the party is easier to hit. LOWERS DAMAGE: as in the DOS game, the party's weapon damage instead.
strings.option.p1.payout-remainder.desc: When XP and gold are split equally on entering a town, what happens to the amount that doesn't divide evenly. FIRST SURVIVOR: it goes to the first living member. LOST: it is thrown away, as the DOS game does.
strings.option.p1.attack-gate.desc: Whether ATTACK and SLASH need weapon skill. ANY SKILL: anyone can use them, as the manual describes (ATTACK 2 swings, SLASH 3 or 4). SKILL NEEDED: as in DOS, low skill turns ATTACK into THRUST and SLASH into ATTACK, so no level 1 character gets past THRUST.
strings.option.p1.lunge.desc: Who can LUNGE at a monster in rank 2. FIGHTERS: fighters only, as the manual says; anyone else thrusts at rank 1 instead. FIGHTERS, THIEVES: the DOS game lets thieves lunge too.
strings.option.p1.binding.desc: How BINDING changes a monster's defense. ALWAYS HELPS: bound monsters are always easier to hit, as the manual says. SCALES DEFENSE: the DOS formula scales defense toward zero, which makes monsters with negative defense harder to hit.
strings.option.p1.confusion-iv.desc: How well CONFUSION IV stops monster spells and special attacks. STOPS SPELLS: victims can't use them at all, as the manual says. 5% OF NORMAL: as in DOS, they keep 5% of their usual chance, which only matters for the strongest casters.
strings.option.p1.fear.desc: What FEAR does. MONSTERS RUN: after the DOS roll lowers their level, the monsters run away, as the manual says (the party keeps kill XP and their gold). LEVEL DROP ONLY: as in DOS, it only lowers the monsters' level by 6; mostly useful before DISSOLVE.
strings.option.p1.dispell-undead.desc: Which monsters DISPELL UNDEAD can affect. UNDEAD ONLY: skeletons, zombies, ghosts and other undead, as the manual says. XP DIVISIBLE BY 7: the DOS test, which also catches BANTIR, DEMON and HIGH DEMON.
strings.option.p1.spell-level.desc: Whether the caster's experience level counts in the roll for CONFUSION, WEAKNESS, BINDING and SLEEP. COUNTS: higher-level casters do better against lower-level monsters, as the manual says. IGNORED: the DOS roll uses only magic power against the target.
strings.option.p1.fireflash-damage.desc: How much damage FIREFLASH does. MANUAL RANGES: the manual's 1-10 / 1-30 / 1-60 / 1-100, scaled down below INT 18. DOS FORMULA: the DOS formula, which gives less (1-9 / 1-26 / 1-52 / 1-90 at INT 18).
strings.option.p1.fireflash-target.desc: Which monster FIREFLASH hits. FRONT RANK: a monster in the front rank, the 'monster close to the spellcaster' of the manual. BACK RANK: as in DOS, the rearmost group, never its last monster.
strings.option.p1.failed-run.desc: What happens to sleeping monsters when their attempt to run away fails. SLEEPERS STAY ASLEEP: they stay asleep. WAKES SLEEPERS: as in the DOS game, every monster wakes up.
strings.option.p1.town-inn-time.desc: How long a rest at a town Inn takes. TWO WEEKS: as the manual says, so the party ages with each stay. NO TIME: as in the DOS game, resting is instant and nobody ages.
strings.option.p1.hit-dice.desc: How many hit points characters gain when created and at each level-up. MANUAL CHART: matches the manual's hit point chart. DOS DICE: the DOS formula, which averages a little lower (2 HP low at level 1, about 5% low by level 15).
strings.option.p1.wild-inn-time.desc: How long a stay at a wilderness inn takes. TWO WEEKS: as the manual says, and the party ages. ABOUT 4 DAYS: as in the DOS game, the stay only advances the travel clock by about four days and ages nobody.
strings.option.p1.inn-magic-cap.desc: How far a wilderness inn can raise a spellcaster's maximum magic points. NEVER PAST TABLE: never above the manual's maximum for class and level. CAN GO 1 PAST: as in DOS, 1% of stays at the maximum raise it one point past.
strings.option.p1.wild-inn-dead.desc: Whether a wilderness inn restores dead members' stored HP and MP. REFILLED: yes, like a town Inn, as the manual says; they stay dead. SKIPPED: as in DOS, dead members are left as they are.
strings.option.p1.pool-cap.desc: How far a magical pool can raise an attribute. RACE MAXIMUM: never past the race maximum from the manual's table. NO CAP: as in the DOS game, with no limit, so several pools can push a stat past the race maximum and past 22.
strings.option.p1.path-time.desc: How long a step on a path takes. FASTEST: twice as fast as any other terrain, as the manual says paths are quicker. AS WATER: the DOS cost, the same as water and bridges, but still quicker than other land.
strings.option.p1.monster-eval.desc: What MONSTER EVALUATION reports. NEARBY MONSTERS: the rough level of the monsters that can be met here, sometimes off by one, as the manual says. TERRAIN FORMULA: the DOS formula, from the map square or dungeon level alone, with no look at real monsters.
strings.option.p1.vision.desc: How much of the map VISION reveals. WHOLE REGION: the whole current wilderness region, for the manual's 'hundreds of miles'. 1-3 SQUARES: as in DOS, only a small square around the party, 1 to 3 squares out depending on magic points left.
strings.option.p1.add-aging.desc: Whether adding a member to the party at the Guild ages them. OTHER TOWNS: only a member who travels from another town ages the 2 months. EVERY ADD: as in DOS, every added member ages 2 months, even one already in this town.
strings.option.p1.cast-flag.desc: Which spells count toward the Inn's chance to raise maximum magic points. ANY CAST: any spell cast since the last rest, as the manual says. COMBAT ONLY: as in the DOS game, only spells cast in combat count; healing in town or the field does not.
strings.option.p1.dungeon-map-no.desc: What answering NO to 'SAVE THE DUNGEON MAP?' on leaving a dungeon does. FORGETS SAVED MAP: any saved map of this dungeon is erased, so the next visit starts fresh. KEEPS OLD SAVE: as in DOS, nothing is written, so an older saved map of it can come back.
strings.option.p1.halfling-dex.desc: The highest DEX a Halfling can have. 20: the manual's race table. 19: the DOS game's tables, where every Halfling DEX roll is one lower.
strings.option.p1.guild-size.desc: How many characters the Guild can hold. 21: the manual's maximum. 22: the DOS game fills every Guild record.
strings.option.p1.lifespans.desc: How long each race lives before old age kills it. MANUAL: the manual's figures (elves about 3000 years, dwarves and gnomes 200, humans 80, others 40-50). DOS FACTORS: the DOS formula, which gives halflings and pixies far longer lives and elves shorter ones.
strings.option.p1.monk-sleep.desc: Whether Monks can learn SLEEP. NEVER: the manual's spell table gives Monks no SLEEP. LEVEL 7: the DOS table lets Monks learn it at level 7.
strings.option.p1.town-healing.desc: How much a HEALING spell cast in town heals. 1-9 1-27 ...: the manual's ranges, the same everywhere. 0-10 0-28 ...: the DOS town formula, which can heal nothing; in combat and the field DOS uses the manual's ranges.
strings.option.p1.beg-mercy.desc: Whether BEG FOR MERCY always lets the party go. ALWAYS WORKS: the party hands over gold and some items and goes free, as the manual says. CAN FAIL: as in DOS, it depends on the monsters' mood; on a miss 'MONSTERS DON'T RESPOND' and the fight goes on.
strings.option.p1.sack-size.desc: How many found items the party can carry. 90: as the manual says. 60: the DOS game's limit.
strings.option.p1.sleep.desc: How the SLEEP spell works. LASTS: one roll per monster group; sleepers stay asleep over later rounds until they wake by chance, as the manual describes. THIS ROUND: as in DOS, each monster resists by its own level and a slept monster only loses the rest of the round.
strings.option.p1.charm.desc: What a successful CHARM does. ENDS THE FIGHT: the monsters forget the combat and it ends, as the manual says (kill XP kept, no gold or treasure). +15 REACTION: as in DOS, they only grow friendlier and GREETINGS can be tried again; the fight goes on.
strings.option.p1.teleport.desc: How TELEPORTATION works in combat. ALWAYS, AT ONCE: the party escapes safely right away, as the manual says. CAN FAIL: as in DOS, it can fail, and even when it works the rest of the round plays out before the party escapes.
strings.option.p1.wild-treasure.desc: Whether monsters beaten (or surrendering) in the wilderness leave treasure. ALWAYS: always, as the manual says. LEVEL-BASED CHANCE: as in DOS, only on a roll that improves with the monsters' level; also keeps a DOS bug that lets FIRE ELEMENTALs drop the endgame scroll.
strings.option.p1.summon-party.desc: How many party members SUMMON ELEMENTAL needs. SIX MEMBERS: six living members, as the manual says. 6, THEN 5: the DOS test, which wants six early in a round but only five once a monster has acted. Under 6, THEN 5 the summon also writes DOS's list of targets the way DOS does (see MONSTER SPELL TARGETS).
strings.option.p1.monster-spell-target.desc: Whom a monster spell that hits one member can strike. ANY LIVING MEMBER: any member still alive, equally likely (the manual gives no rule). DOS LIST: DOS's own list of targets, which is only refreshed at certain moments: early in a round the last member in it can't be hit, and after a summon with SUMMON ELEMENTAL NEEDS set to 6, THEN 5 a spell can land on a dead member and do nothing.
strings.option.p1.combat-shares.desc: How XP and gold are reported and kept after a fight. TOTALS: the whole XP and gold are shown and saved to be divided in town, as the manual says. SURVIVOR SHARES: as in DOS, each survivor's share is shown and leftovers that don't divide evenly are lost.
strings.option.p1.continue.desc: What CONTINUE SAVED GAME asks. ASKS GUILD NUMBER: you give the Guild number of a character and play that character's party, so several parties can be out at once, as the manual says. LOADS SAVED PARTY: as in DOS, it asks nothing and loads the one saved party.
strings.option.p1.cast-list.desc: Which spells the Cast command offers outside combat. ALLOWED HERE: only spells that work where the party is, as the manual says. EVERY SPELL: as in DOS, every known spell; one that does nothing here still uses up its magic points.
strings.option.p1.transport-list.desc: Which towns TRANSPORTATION offers. OTHER TOWNS: every town but the one the party is in. ALL 12 TOWNS: as in DOS, the current town is listed too, and picking it re-enters it.
strings.option.p1.combat-spell-list.desc: Which spells a caster can pick in combat. COMBAT SPELLS: only combat and anywhere spells; the manual marks the others non-combat. EVERY SPELL: as in DOS, every known spell; a non-combat one cast in combat uses up its magic points and does nothing.
strings.option.p1.orders-reset.desc: Whether each member's combat order carries over between trips. KEPT: orders stay until you change them, as the manual says. RESET TO PARRY: as in DOS, everyone goes back to PARRY on leaving town and after a party defeat.
strings.option.p2.transfer-spells.desc: Which classes start Phantasie II with a spell when a party is brought over from Phantasie I. WIZARD, PRIEST: only Wizards keep spell #5 and Priests spell #1, as the manual says. ALSO RANGER, MONK: as the Atari ST, Rangers also get HEALING I and Monks FIREFLASH I.
strings.option.p2.transfer-divine.desc: Which divine spells a character keeps when brought over from Phantasie I; every other spell is lost. #55 AND UP keeps both DIVINE I and DIVINE II, as the transfer text and the Atari ST do. #58 AND UP follows the manual's other page and drops DIVINE II.
strings.option.p2.transfer-gold.desc: What happens to a character's bank gold when brought over from Phantasie I. ST FORMULA: the Atari ST's fixed formula, so most end with about 100 GP and a poor character can even gain gold. NEVER GAINS: the same formula, but nobody ends with more than they had.
strings.option.p2.training-cost.desc: What the Guild tells a character who lacks the experience to train. ALWAYS SHOWN: the XP still needed and the cost of training, as the manual says. ONLY WITH ENOUGH XP: as the Atari ST, only the XP needed; the cost appears once the XP is there.
strings.option.p2.hit-dice.desc: How many hit points a character gains on a level-up. MANUAL CHART: rolls that follow the manual's Hit Points by Class and Level chart. ST DICE: the Atari ST's smaller roll, which leaves characters below the chart, as in Phantasie I's original code.
strings.option.p2.wizard-resurrection.desc: Whether Wizards can learn RESURRECTION. LEVEL 13: a Wizard learns it at level 13, as the manual's mortality text says a high-level wizard can raise the dead. NEVER: as the Atari ST and the manual's spell tables, only Priests and Rangers ever learn it.
strings.option.p2.autosave.desc: When leaving a town saves the game. TOWN OPTION: only while the Auto save item in the Town options is ticked (off at start), as the Atari ST. ALWAYS: every time the party leaves a town, as the manual's Apple section describes.
strings.option.p2.gold-cap.desc: The most gold the party purse and each bank account can hold. 65,000: the manual's limit. 65,535: the Atari ST's limit.
strings.option.p2.guild-size.desc: How many characters the Guild can hold. 21: the manual's limit. 22: the Atari ST fills all 22 of its slots. GUILD ROSTER LIMIT can lift the cap altogether.
strings.option.p2.lifespans.desc: How long each race lives before aging and dying of old age. MANUAL AGES: the manual's lifespans (elves about 3000 years, humans about 80 and so on), give or take 10%. ST RACE FACTORS: the Atari ST's formula, so a human dies at about 88 to 137.
strings.option.p2.dispell-undead.desc: Which monsters DISPELL UNDEAD can affect. UNDEAD ONLY: the skeletons, zombies, ghosts and other undead, including Pluto's Undead Snake. XP DIVISIBLE BY 7: the Atari ST's test, which also hits some demons and misses the snake.
strings.option.p2.fear.desc: What the FEAR spell does. MONSTERS RUN: it frightens monsters into running away, as the manual says. LEVEL DROP ONLY: as the Atari ST, nothing runs; a successful cast only makes the encounter weaker.
strings.option.p2.fear-bosses.desc: Whether FEAR can frighten off Pluto, his Ice Dragon and his eight minions when FEAR makes monsters run. STAND FAST: they never run, as Phantasie I's Black Lord. RUN: they can be frightened off like any other monster.
strings.option.p2.transport-list.desc: Which towns the TRANSPORTATION spell can reach. ANY OTHER TOWN: every other town in Ferronrah and the Netherworld, as the manual says. SAME PLANE: as the Atari ST, only towns on the same plane, so the spell never crosses between Ferronrah and the Netherworld.
strings.option.p2.inn-dead.desc: Whether a town Inn stay restores the hit points and magic of DEAD party members (they stay dead either way). REFILLED: every member is refilled, as in Phantasie I. SKIPPED: as the Atari ST, dead members are left as they were and are 'resting in peace'.
strings.option.p2.town-inn-time.desc: How long a stay at a town Inn takes. TWO WEEKS: about two weeks pass and the party ages, as the manual says. NO TIME: as the Atari ST, the stay takes no time and ages nobody.
strings.option.p2.inn-magic-cap.desc: Whether resting at a wilderness inn can raise a character's maximum magic points past the manual's table. UP TO THE TABLE: the raise stops at the table. 1% CHANCE PAST TABLE: as the Atari ST, a character at the table has a 1% chance per stay to go one point past it.
strings.option.p2.wild-inn-time.desc: How long a stay at an inn out in the wilderness takes. TWO WEEKS: the party ages two weeks, as the manual says. TRAVEL TIME, NO AGING: as the Atari ST, the stay only adds some travel time and ages nobody directly.
strings.option.p2.combat-shares.desc: How experience and gold are shown after a fight. PARTY TOTALS: the whole amount is shown and pooled, then divided when the party enters a town, as the manual says. PER SURVIVOR: as the Atari ST, each survivor's share is shown and leftover remainders are lost.
strings.option.p2.path-time.desc: How long a step along a path takes in the wilderness. FASTEST: paths are quicker than any other terrain, as the manual says. AS WATER: as the Atari ST, a path step costs the same as water, quicker than land but not the fastest.
strings.option.p2.dungeon-map-no.desc: What answering NO to 'save the dungeon map?' on leaving a dungeon does. FORGETS OLD SAVE: an earlier saved map of that dungeon is dropped, so it starts fresh next time. KEEPS OLD SAVE: as the Atari ST, the earlier saved map comes back on the next visit.
strings.option.guild-limit.desc: How many characters the Guild roster can hold, in every game. GAME'S OWN CAP: the game's original limit (see GUILD SIZE). NO LIMIT: the roster keeps growing past it. An export to an original save writes only the first 22 and lists the rest.
strings.option.treasury.desc: One gold pool for the whole Guild, in place of each character's bank account and the party purse. Every party member can spend it at any time, in town or in the field; the Bank shows the balance and a ledger. OFF: the game's own purse and bank accounts. TRIP GOLD AT RISK: gold won since the party left town is carried until it is back in a town, and begging, surrender or an event can still take it; the savings are safe. NOTHING AT RISK: every gain goes straight into the treasury. Lifts the gold cap. Transfers to another game give each character an even share.
strings.core.treasury.title: GUILD TREASURY
strings.option.elemental-load.desc: When Guild Add lets an elemental join the party, in Phantasie I, II and III. GAME'S OWN RULE: I needs six characters and nobody can be added after it; II needs none and characters can still join; III needs one character and more can be added in front of it. AS PHANTASIE I or AS PHANTASIE III: that game's rule in every game. Summon Elemental in a fight keeps the game's own rule (I and II: a party of six), and I still unloads the elemental on entering a town. An elemental is never removed from the game: it can always be added again.
strings.option.elemental-drop.desc: What Guild Drop of a character does to a loaded elemental, in Phantasie I, II and III. GAME'S OWN RULE: I unloads it on every Drop; II keeps it, even with no character left; III keeps it while a character is left. ELEMENTAL LEAVES: Phantasie I's rule in every game. STAYS WHILE ONE LEFT: Phantasie III's rule in every game. In II and III, Drop can also unload the elemental itself. An unloaded elemental goes back to the Guild and can be added again.
strings.option.elemental-purge.desc: What Guild Purge of a character who is in the party does, in Phantasie I, II and III. GAME'S OWN RULE: I purges the character and unloads the elemental; II purges it and keeps the elemental; III follows the rules preset: AS DROP under Manual, Remaster and Custom, REFUSED under Original. ELEMENTAL LEAVES: purged, the elemental is unloaded (Phantasie I). AS DROP: purged, the elemental does what DROP WITH ELEMENTAL says (III's manual). REFUSED: a party member can't be purged; drop it first (DOS III). An elemental itself can never be purged.
strings.option.p3.slash-fallback.desc: What a Slash turns into when the fighter's Attack % is under 150. ATTACKS: it becomes a normal two-swing Attack (which itself drops to a Thrust below 76). THRUSTS: it becomes a single Thrust straight away, as DOS does.
strings.option.p3.lunge.desc: Who may choose Lunge in combat. FIGHTERS ONLY: only Fighters can Lunge, as the manual says. FIGHTERS + THIEVES: Thieves get the Lunge option too, as in DOS.
strings.option.p3.thief-attack.desc: Whether a Thief can aim the Attack option at a rear rank. ANY RANK: a Thief picks the target rank for Attack just as for Thrust and Slash. RANK 1 ONLY: Attack always hits the front rank, as DOS does.
strings.option.p3.aim.desc: The Aim blow's requirements and chance to hit. ATTACK 150, HALF %: Aim needs an Attack % of 150 or more (else it becomes a Thrust) and hits at half the Attack %. ALWAYS, FULL %: anyone can Aim, at the full Attack %, as in DOS.
strings.option.p3.down-targets.desc: How easy it is to hit someone who is Down or Out (for monsters, also Unconscious). DOUBLE, MAX 95%: double the normal chance, at most 95%. ALWAYS HIT: every blow lands, as in DOS. Sleeping targets are always hit either way.
strings.option.p3.armour-defence.desc: How armour affects a monster's melee chance to hit a character. PROTECTS: more armour makes you harder to hit, as the manual says. HELPS MONSTERS HIT: DOS's reversed sign, where more armour makes monsters hit you more often.
strings.option.p3.arrow-flame.desc: How Arrow Flame I and II boost a bow. ADDS TO BOW POINTS: they add 15 or 25 to the bow's points, which feed the normal damage formula. REPLACES DAMAGE: the damage becomes the bow's points plus 15 or 25, as DOS does.
strings.option.p3.parry.desc: How the Parry action works. SKILL ROLL, BLOCKS HIT: this round's Parry rolls the Parry skill; a success lowers monsters' melee chances by the shield's points and softens the first hit. SAVED FROM LAST FIGHT: DOS's rule, where a Parry as last action of the previous fight gives the shield bonus all fight.
strings.option.p3.status-letter.desc: The letter shown for an unconscious monster in combat. U: as the manual. O: as DOS shows it. Display only; nothing else changes.
strings.option.p3.combat-spell-list.desc: Which spells a caster can pick in combat. COMBAT SPELLS: only combat and anywhere spells; the manual marks the others non-combat. EVERY SPELL: as in DOS, every known spell is listed; picking a non-combat one is refused with a message and the character thrusts instead, spending no magic points.
strings.option.p3.healing-iv.desc: How many cure points the Healing IV spell and Healing Potion 10 spend on injuries. 6 CURE POINTS: the manual's amount. 4 CURE POINTS: DOS's smaller amount.
strings.option.p3.heal-order.desc: Which body area a healing spell or potion cures first. MOST VITAL FIRST: each cure goes to the worst area it can fix, the most vital first among equals, starting over every time. ROUND ROBIN: DOS's pass that moves on to the next area after each cure.
strings.option.p3.inn-healing.desc: How much an inn stay heals injuries. 1 BREAK OR 2 INJURIES: every stay mends one broken area or two injured ones, as the manual says. TOWN INN: FULL CURE: a town inn sets every area that is not Gone back to Okay, as DOS does.
strings.option.p3.hit-points.desc: How hit points are rolled when a character gains a level. BY CONSTITUTION: hit dice scale with Constitution, as in Phantasie I (Constitution 10 matches the chart). CLASS AND LEVEL: Constitution is ignored, as in DOS.
strings.option.p3.level-gold.desc: Whether a character is paid for gaining a level. SOCIAL CLASS X 256: each level gained puts social class times 256 gold into that character's bank account, as the manual says. NONE: no gold, as in DOS.
strings.option.p3.encounter-block.desc: Whether Greet, Beg for Mercy, Accept Surrender, monsters fleeing and the party's Flee work against the stronger monsters. ANY MONSTER: they work against every monster. NOT MONSTERS 44+: DOS blocks them when the front monster is number 44 or higher.
strings.option.p3.boss-flee.desc: Whether the party can flee from the final bosses, Nikademus and Lord Wood. NO: Flee is blocked against them, as in every original version. YES: they can be fled like any other monster.
strings.option.p3.mercy.desc: What monsters take when they accept a Beg for Mercy. GOLD + NEW ITEMS 50%: all the party's gold, plus each item found since leaving town with a 50% chance. GOLD ONLY: just the gold, as every original version does.
strings.option.p3.found-items.desc: How many items the party's found-item list can hold before new finds are lost. 90: the manual's limit. UNLIMITED: no limit. 60: DOS's limit.
strings.option.p3.bank.desc: How Deposit splits the party's gold among the members' accounts. SHARES 1-3, FEE: each member gets 1, 2 or 3 shares and a small banking fee is lost, as the manual says. SHARES 1-3, NO FEE: the same shares with no fee. EVEN SPLIT: DOS's equal split, with Withdraw all gold.
strings.option.p3.gold-cap.desc: Whether gold has a ceiling. 65,000: party gold and each bank account stop at 65,000, as the manual says. NONE: no limit, as in DOS.
strings.option.p3.trade.desc: The Trade Items option. GIVE AND SELL: give an item to another member or sell it at the Distribute price, as the manual says. GIVE ONLY: giving but no selling, as on the Amiga. NO: DOS has no Trade Items at all.
strings.option.p3.armory-restock.desc: Whether the Armory's stock changes on its own. EVERY VISIT: weapons and potions are re-rolled each time the party enters a town. NEVER: the stock only changes by buying and selling, as in DOS.
strings.option.p3.autosave.desc: When the game saves itself. LEAVING TOWN: it saves automatically each time the party leaves a town, as the manual says. MENU ONLY: it saves only when you choose Save from the menu, as in DOS.
strings.option.p3.roster.desc: How many characters the Guild can hold. UNLIMITED: no limit, as the manual suggests. 17 + 3 ELEMENTALS: DOS's 20 slots, three of them taken by the elementals. The general Guild limit option can lift this too.
strings.option.p3.skill-tables.desc: Five entries in III's skill-training tables look like data errors (for example Ranger Attack at level 15). TYPOS FIXED (AS I): those five use Phantasie I's values. AS DOS READS THEM: training uses DOS's tables exactly as stored.
strings.option.p3.bow-spells.desc: What happens when several bow spells are cast on the same character. NEVER LOWER: a later spell never lowers the Fire Bow % or damage an earlier one gave. LAST ONE SETS: the last spell cast sets the Fire Bow %, even if lower, as in DOS.
strings.option.p3.altar.desc: The altar in the Pendragon archive, whose text says it grants Divine Aid. GRANTS DIVINE AID: it teaches the spell, as its text says. INJURES TORSOS: DOS's data fault, which injures every living member's torso and grants no spell.
strings.option.p3.event-gold.desc: Gold given or taken by dungeon events. AS WRITTEN: amounts are read correctly. DOS BUG (WIZARD PAYS): DOS misreads large amounts, so instead of taking 65,280 gold at the end, the Gnome wizard gives the party 256 gold.
strings.option.p3.lifespans.desc: Whether characters age. DECLINE AND DEATH: characters get Phantasie I's lifespans, weaken past 70% of theirs and die of old age past it, checked on entering town. NONE: no ageing, as DOS never checks age.
strings.option.p3.dungeon-map-no.desc: What answering NO to 'Would you like to save this map?' does when leaving a dungeon. OLD MAP FORGOTTEN: the dungeon's saved map is dropped, so the next visit starts fresh. OLD MAP KEPT: an earlier saved map stays, as DOS writes nothing.
strings.option.p3.transfer-source.desc: Which games' characters the game menu's transfer can bring into Phantasie III. PHANTASIE I OR II: either, as the manual says. PHANTASIE I ONLY: as DOS, which reads only Phantasie I's roster.
strings.option.p3.transfer-roster.desc: What a transfer does to the characters already in Phantasie III. ADDED: the newcomers join the Guild and everyone stays, as DOS does. ERASED FIRST: every Phantasie III character, the party too, is erased before the transfer, as the manual's text says.
strings.option.p3.transfer-level.desc: The level transferred characters start at. Either way they keep 100 experience per old level. LEVEL 0: everyone, as the manual says; the first training costs and needs what level 1's does. LEVEL 1, UNDEAD 20: as DOS, where an Undead character arrives at level 20.
strings.option.p3.transfer-divine.desc: What happens to DIVINE I and DIVINE II on a transfer. KEPT AS DIVINE AID: the character knows Divine Aid, Phantasie III's divine spell, as the manual keeps divine spells. LOST: as DOS, which keeps no spell but the class's first one.
strings.option.p3.transfer-wand.desc: Whether the Wand of Nikademus comes along. KEPT: when anyone in the old roster held it (a Phantasie I score above 99), every transferred character carries the wand, as the manual says and the Apple II version does. LOST: as DOS, which brings no item.
strings.option.p3.transport-planes.desc: Where the Transportation spell can take the party. SCANDOR ONLY: the 14 towns of Scandor, as in the original game; from a plane town it is the way home. VISITED PLANE TOWNS: also Light, Dark and Death once someone in the party has been there, so the party can return without walking the planes again.
strings.option.p4.nikademus.desc: Whether Nikademus, hero of the earlier games, can be chosen as an ancestor when creating a character in the Hall of Glory. ALLOWED (AS HUMAN) lets him be an ancestor, counting as a Human for the race mix. NOT POSSIBLE follows the X68000 code: any combination with him is refused.
strings.option.p4.social-bias.desc: How Elves and Dwarves roll their social class at creation. Class sets starting gold and level-up gold. OFTEN HIGH follows the manual: they roll 10 points higher, so nobles are about twice as common. SAME AS OTHER RACES follows the X68000 code: no bonus.
strings.option.p4.strides.desc: The base stride (movement speed) of Halflings and Orcs, which also sets how far Levitation lasts. 5 / 8 follows the manual: Halflings 5, Orcs 8. 6 / 7 follows the X68000 code: Halflings 6, Orcs 7.
strings.option.p4.gargoyle-classes.desc: Which classes a Gargoyle character may take. THIEF/FIGHTER/GARGOYLE follows the manual. GARGOYLE ONLY follows the X68000 code, which allows only the Gargoyle class.
strings.option.p4.priest-levels.desc: How far Priests can train. 35, EVERY SPELL follows the manual: Priests go 5 levels past the others, to 35, learning their missing spells at levels 31-35 until they know all 65. 30 LIKE OTHERS follows the X68000 code: they stop at 30 with 35 spells.
strings.option.p4.fighter-spells.desc: How many spells a Fighter learns while training. 4 SPELLS follows the manual: only the first 4 minor spells (Strength 1, Monster Evaluation, Strength 2, Accuracy). 7 SPELLS follows the X68000 code, which adds Strength 3 and 4 and Arrow Flame 1.
strings.option.p4.thief-hp.desc: How many hit points Thieves gain per level. FEWEST OF ALL follows the manual: always 1 below the lowest other class at that level. X68000 TABLE follows the code's table, where Wizards can have fewer HP than Thieves.
strings.option.p4.level-wrap.desc: What training does at level 15 (not yet decided, D4-060). GO ON TO 30 follows the MSX2 code and the manual's higher levels: 16, 17 and up. 15 TRAINS TO 1 follows the X68000 code, which writes (level + 1) mod 15, so a level-15 character drops to level 1.
strings.option.p4.long-sword.desc: The Long Sword's weapon value. 14 POINTS follows the manual; 13 POINTS follows the X68000 code and the item catalogue.
strings.option.p4.town-entry.desc: What happens when the party enters a town. GOLD TO BANK + XP follows the manual: the party's gold is paid into the members' bank accounts by shares you choose, then experience is shared out. XP ONLY follows the X68000 code: only experience is shared and the gold stays in the purse.
strings.option.p4.inn-time.desc: Whether resting at a town inn passes time (which matters for aging). TWO WEEKS follows the manual: each stay takes two weeks. NO TIME follows the X68000 code.
strings.option.p4.resale.desc: The price a shop asks for an item the party sold it. PAID + 25% follows the manual: 25% more than the shop paid for it. FULL PRICE follows the X68000 code: the shop's normal price.
strings.option.p4.lifespans.desc: How long each race lives before growing old and dying. MANUAL BY RACE uses the manual's ages (Elf about 2,000 years, Dwarf and Gnome 200, Human 80, others about 45), varied a little by Luck. X68000 LUCK RULE uses the code's Luck-based formula, under which Elves never die, and, as the original does, takes a new character's starting age from the race of the first guild slot.
strings.option.p4.potion-wounds.desc: How much healing potions heal. MANUAL TABLE follows the manual's tables for HP and wounds. ONE STEP LOWER follows the X68000 code: potions 1, 4, 7 and 10 heal one wound step less (potion 1 heals no wound) and potion 6 gives 36 HP instead of 35.
strings.option.p4.strikes.desc: How many strikes the Attack and Slash combat commands make. 2 / 3-4 STRIKES follows the manual: Attack strikes twice at -10 to hit and Slash 3-4 times at -20, each strike for full damage. ONE HIT ROLL follows the X68000 code: every action is one hit and one damage roll.
strings.option.p4.aim-blow.desc: Where the Aim Blow combat command lands. HEAD OR TORSO follows the manual: a hit always strikes the head (25%) or torso (75%), so it can kill or stun outright. -15 TO HIT ONLY follows the code: just a harder-to-land blow that hits like any other.
strings.option.p4.head-torso.desc: What happens to a party member whose head or torso is lost. KILLS follows the manual: the character dies whatever its HP. OUT, HEALABLE follows the X68000 code: the character is Out but alive and can be healed back.
strings.option.p4.throwing.desc: Which skill thrown weapons use. THROWING SKILL follows the manual: throws use the Throwing skill. FIRE BOW SKILL follows the X68000 code: throws use Fire Bow, and Throwing has no effect.
strings.option.p4.party-arrow-flame.desc: What the Party Arrow Flame spell boosts for the whole party's bows. HIT + DAMAGE follows the manual: better hit chance and more damage. DAMAGE ONLY follows the X68000 code: no hit bonus.
strings.option.p4.weakness.desc: What the Weakness spell lowers in the monsters. LESS DAMAGE follows the manual: their attacks do less damage. LESS DEFENCE follows the X68000 code: the party hits them more easily instead.
strings.option.p4.flameball.desc: Where the Flameball spell burns. AROUND CASTER follows the manual: everyone near the caster, friend or foe, is hit, except those in strong body armour. AROUND TARGET follows the X68000 code: a pattern around the chosen square, and armour only reduces the damage.
strings.option.p4.spell-damage.desc: How much Fire Flash and Mind Blast hurt and the Healing spell heals. FLAT 1 TO MAX follows the manual: from 1 up to the listed amount. X68000 ROLLS follows the code: Fire Flash scales with Intelligence, Mind Blast falls 1 short and misses some monsters, and Healing can heal 0.
strings.option.p4.annihilate.desc: What spell 64, Annihilate Enemy, does in combat. NO EFFECT follows every original: the caster says the spell and loses all MP, nothing else happens. DIVINE STRIKE is the remaster's own effect (no original has one): the caster pours all MP into it and every enemy on the field takes 2 to 4 times that much damage, with no resistance, immunity or armour; the party is never hit. MP drops to 0 either way.
strings.option.p4.spell-wording.desc: How the Slow, Fear and Dissolve spells work. AS MANUAL DESCRIBES: Slow 2 cuts enemy stride to 3/4, Fear makes the enemy flee, Dissolve deals its damage over 3 rounds. X68000 CODE: Slow 2 cuts stride to 1/4, Fear only lowers the encounter level, Dissolve hits at once.
strings.option.p4.teleport.desc: Where the Teleportation spell takes the party. PREVIOUS SQUARE sends it back to the square it came from. RANDOM SQUARE sends it to a random open square on the same level or outdoor area. ENTRANCE sends it to the dungeon's entrance. X68000 CODE does what the original code does: back to the previous square outdoors, but in a dungeon the party stays where it fought.
strings.option.p4.mp-costs.desc: The magic points a few spells cost (Slow, Arrow Flame, Party Arrow Flame, Dissolve). AS IN MANUAL uses the costs printed in the manual. X68000 TABLE uses the code's table, which differs for those spells.
strings.option.p4.auto-spells.desc: Which spells characters cast on their own in auto combat. MANUAL LIST uses only the spells the manual lists. X68000 LIST uses the code's lists, which add Confusion, Party Arrow Flame, Party Accuracy, Mind Blast and Awaken but never cast Sleep or Dissolve.
strings.option.p4.night-watch.desc: What a night watch with good hearing (Listen) does when monsters attack the camp. WAKES PARTY follows the manual: the whole party is woken before the fight. STOPS SURPRISE ONLY follows the X68000 code: it only cancels the monsters' free first round.
strings.option.p4.beg-mercy.desc: What the party gives up when begging for mercy works. ALL GOLD + ITEMS follows the manual: all the party's gold plus one random unequipped item from each member. KEEPS UP TO 255 GOLD follows the X68000 code: no items are taken and some gold is left.
strings.option.p4.spot-item.desc: How treasure is found after a fight. FINDS TREASURE follows the manual: members roll their Spot Item skill (50+ also identifies the find); outdoor wins and dungeon surrenders get treasure automatically. FLAT CHANCE follows the X68000 code, which ignores the skill.
strings.option.p4.identify.desc: Whether the Identify spell always works. MAY FAIL follows the manual: it succeeds 50% of the time plus 5% per caster level. ALWAYS follows the X68000 code.
strings.option.p4.monster-eval.desc: Whether the Monster Evaluation spell can misreport the monsters' level. SOMETIMES WRONG follows the manual: it is off by 1 level on 50% of casts minus 5% per caster level (at least 10%). ALWAYS RIGHT follows the X68000 code.
strings.option.p4.cast-places.desc: Which spells the C (cast) menu offers in town, outdoors and in dungeons (not yet decided, D4-061). MANUAL'S LISTS follows the manual's spell pages: Levitation only in the wilds or dungeons, Divine Aid also outdoors. X68000 LISTS follows the code: Levitation also in town, Divine Aid only in dungeons.
strings.option.p4.party-info.desc: What the P (party info) page shows outdoors. SINCE TOWN follows the manual: the experience and gold the party has gained since it left town. X68000 CODE follows the original code: a tenth of the experience gained and all the gold the party carries.
strings.option.p4.levitation.desc: How long Levitation lasts outside combat. 5 X STRIDE STEPS follows the manual: 5 times the slowest member's stride in steps, outdoors and in dungeons. UNTIL A FIGHT follows the X68000 code: it lasts until the next fight but only works in dungeons.
strings.option.p4.navigation.desc: How risky sailing is with poor Navigation. The best navigator always steers. EXTRA DRIFT UNDER 50 follows the manual's warning: below 50 the ship has an added chance to drift off course each step. NORMAL DRIFT ONLY follows the X68000 code.
strings.option.p4.ship-wear.desc: Whether ships can be lost. WRECK AND WEAR follows the manual: a ship may be wrecked (5%) after a sea fight the party loses or flees, and wears out after many sea steps (see SHIP LIFE). NEVER follows the X68000 code: fights and use never harm the ship.
strings.option.p4.ship-life.desc: How many sea steps a ship lasts before it wears out, when SHIP WEAR is set to WRECK AND WEAR. Choose 4000 STEPS, 2000 STEPS or 8000 STEPS.
strings.option.p4.examine.desc: What the Examine command does in dungeons. PARTY SEARCH follows the manual: the party searches the area, getting +20 to find traps and treasure. AUTO WALK follows the X68000 code: the party walks around on its own for up to 63 steps with fewer encounters.
strings.option.p4.map-step.desc: What pressing M (the wide 3 x 3 map) does outdoors. VIEW ONLY follows the manual: it just switches the view. ALSO TAKES A STEP follows the X68000 code: each switch replays the current square, so time passes and a new encounter roll is made.
strings.option.p4.overview.desc: Which 3 x 3 maps the wide map (M) shows outdoors. FIXED BLOCKS follows the X68000 code: one of three set blocks that holds the party's map, so the party is often off-centre. CENTRED ON PARTY follows the manual's wording ("the 3 x 3 around the current area"): the party's map in the middle, with black past the edge of the world. In the Netherworld only the party's own map shows either way.
strings.option.p4.dungeon-reload.desc: What loading a game saved in a dungeon does. X68000 CODE does what the original does: its save holds no map, so the dungeon is read fresh from disk (doors, levers and opened chests changed by events come back unless the dungeon's own load event redoes them), the location flags rotate one more step and the dungeon's load event runs again. In a dungeon the game can then be saved only at the command prompt, not in the middle of an event. KEEP SAVED MAP saves the dungeon as it is, events included, and the game goes on exactly where it stopped.
strings.option.p4.transfer-join.desc: Where the Hall of Glory's transfer can put Phantasie III characters. HALL ONLY follows the original and the manual: they enter the Hall and serve only as ancestors. HALL OR GUILD (remaster option) also lets them join the Guild as playable level 1 characters with their race, class and abilities, IV's own skills, hit points and spells, and 100 experience per old level to train up again.
strings.option.p4.transfer-games.desc: Which games' characters the Hall of Glory's transfer reads. PHANTASIE III follows the original. PHANTASIE I, II OR III (remaster option) also takes characters from your Phantasie I and II saves into the Hall as ancestors; one who killed the Black Lord or destroyed the orb counts as having completed that game.
strings.option.p4.gold-cap.desc: The most gold the party purse and each bank account can hold. 65,000 follows the manual on every path (loot, selling, bank, level-up gold), with the original withdraw bug fixed. NONE removes the limit.
strings.option.p4.aging.desc: What happens to a character's abilities on growing older (at 70% of the lifespan). ABILITIES X 0.8 follows the MSX2 code and the manual: each ability and Luck drop to 80%, once. ABILITIES TO 0 keeps the X68000 code's bug, which sets them all to 0.
strings.option.shared-aging.desc: One aging rule for all four games, so a character ages the same wherever it goes. SHARED: the lifespans of the Phantasie I, II and III manuals in every game (Elf about 3,000 years, Dwarf and Gnome 200, Human 80, every other race 40 to 50), varied a little by Luck and fixed when the character is made; past 70% of it the abilities drop to 80% once, past 100% the character dies, checked on entering a town. Age, lifespan and growing older come along unchanged when a character moves to another game. Overrides the game's own LIFESPANS row (and IV's GROWING OLDER). THE GAME'S OWN: each game's own rule.
strings.option.modern-inventory.desc: MODERN: gear stays where you put it. Use the inventory screen (V) anywhere outside combat to wear items, take them off, give them to another member or use the stash, and to sell items while in town. D)ISTRIBUTE shares out gold and experience only and never collects your items, Phantasie III's town entry no longer re-equips everyone or opens the found-item screen, and a new item is worn by itself only when nothing is worn in its slot. Overrides ITEM STASH. ORIGINAL: the original hand-out screens, where every D)ISTRIBUTE collects all items and hands them out again.
strings.game.distribute_modern: Items stay where they are. Press V for the inventory: wear, give, stash, and sell in town.
strings.option.p4.monster-hp.desc: How many hit points monsters get. MSX2 0.5-1.4X follows the MSX2 code: half to 1.4 times their base HP. X68000 1.8X follows the X68000 code, where most monsters get 1.8 times their base HP, making fights much harder.
strings.option.p4.weak-ancestors.desc: What happens when a character's ancestors are very weak (their average ability below 5). WEAK DICE gives the descendant weak rolls, as intended. ALL 6S (BUG) keeps the X68000 code's bug: every die rolls 6, so the descendant gets top abilities.
strings.module.p1.combat-orders.desc: Phantasie I's combat orders: THRUST, ATTACK, SLASH, LUNGE, CAST and PARRY, with party melee and combat spells. ... uses the same set. ON gives the party these orders ...
strings.module.p2.rock-throwing.desc: Phantasie II's Toss Rock order: any member, from any rank, can throw rocks (never used up) that hit on the TOSS skill, which grows at creation and level-up. ON adds the order to this game's combat menu.
strings.module.p4.lineage.desc: Phantasie IV's ancestry at creation: Guild New can make a descendant of two ancestors of the same race, each a new person or a hero from the Hall (IV's Lord Wood and Filmon, the characters on your saves of the other games, the IV save's Hall). Abilities are inherited by IV's rule, then kept inside this game's own limits. Base races only, no mixed races. OFF keeps this game's own creation.

strings.module.p3.combat-actions.desc: Phantasie III's combat: Attack, Lunge, Slash, Thrust, Fire Bow, Parry, Aim and Cast, with party ranks, body-area injuries, bows and III's monster melee. Used by ... only for now.
strings.module.p3.body-part-injury.desc: Phantasie III's injuries: blows hit the head, torso, arms or legs, each Okay, Injured, Broken or Gone, on adventurers and monsters alike. Not built yet as a separate option.
strings.module.p3.bows.desc: Phantasie III's bows: a bow slot, the Fire Bow skill and a Fire order, replacing Phantasie II's rocks. Not built yet as a separate option.
strings.module.p3.aim.desc: Phantasie III's Aim order: one blow aimed at a monster's head or torso, with a lower chance to hit. Not built yet as a separate option.
strings.module.p3.party-ranks.desc: Phantasie III's party ranks: each member stands in the Front, Middle or Back rank, which changes how easily they hit and are hit. Not built yet as a separate option.
